quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: Why should you keep an adequate distance between your vehicle and the one in front of you?

options.text: It gives you time and space to see and react to hazards.
So you can tailgate.
It helps traffic counters count you accurately.
It encourages other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time and space to see and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: A good following distance gives you room to stop or move if the car in front stops suddenly. It also helps you see the road ahead for hazards like potholes.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier because you can see the lights of other vehicles.
Harder because visibility is reduced.
Not allowed on highways.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder because visibility is reduced.
questions.explanation: Night riding is more dangerous because you cannot see as well. Without sunlight and shadows, it is harder to judge distances.

questions.question: Studies show that motorcycles with daytime headlights on are:

options.text: Not as easy to see as other vehicles.
More visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
Confusing to other drivers.
Less safe than with headlights off.

questions.correctAnswerText: More visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever you ride. A motorcycle with its headlight on is twice as likely to be noticed by other drivers.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?

options.text: Before every ride.
Once a week.
Once a month.
Twice a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This takes only a few minutes and helps prevent problems before you enter traffic.

questions.question: What should motorcycle riding clothes cover?

options.text: Your arms and legs completely.
Your arms completely, but not your legs.
Your legs completely, but not your arms.
Whatever feels most comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely for proper protection.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: You can touch your feet to the ground while sitting on it.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars go over your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch your feet to the ground while sitting on it.
questions.explanation: A proper fit means your feet can reach the ground while you sit on the motorcycle. You should be able to easily reach and use all controls.

questions.question: Only ____ can remove alcohol from your body.

options.text: Time
Coffee
Exercise
Fresh air

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time reduces alcohol in your body. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower your blood alcohol level or make you sober. They may keep you awake, but they do not change how much alcohol is in your system.

questions.question: Helmets must be worn by:

options.text: All operators.
All operators under age 18.
All operators who have had their license for less than two years.
Never required.

questions.correctAnswerText: All operators under age 18.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle operators and passengers under 18, and anyone riding on a learner's permit, must wear an approved helmet. All riders should wear a helmet every time they ride.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Ignore them.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up.
Exit the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to move them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only encourage them to tailgate faster.

questions.question: Which of these is a slippery surface?

options.text: Wet pavement
A driveway
Dry pavement
A parking lot

questions.correctAnswerText: Wet pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted markings, and metal road covers are slippery. Ride with extra care on these surfaces.

questions.question: Which surface provides good traction?

options.text: Wet pavement
Dry pavement
Lane markings
Snow

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all reduce tire traction. Dry pavement provides the best traction.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Sturdy boots
Tennis shoes
Shoes with loose laces
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy boots or high-top shoes that support your ankles. Lace-up boots are best. Tuck any long laces away before riding.

questions.question: When riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Test the seat to make sure it is comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good riding condition.
Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
Ride as you usually do, since most bikes are similar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different. Before riding an unfamiliar bike, practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes. Learn where the gears are located.

questions.question: When operating a motorcycle, what must you do?

options.text: You do not need to carry your license with you.
You must carry your license with you.
Your license must be affixed to your helmet.
Your license must be affixed to your right arm.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must carry your license with you.
questions.explanation: You must carry your valid driver license with the correct motorcycle endorsement whenever you ride. You must also carry a learner's permit on every ride if you have one.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Stay where you are to avoid surprising the driver.
Wave at the other driver to get their attention.
Slow down until you are out of the blind spot.
Pull over to the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down until you are out of the blind spot.
questions.explanation: If you are in a vehicle's blind spot, either speed up quickly or slow down to leave the spot.

questions.question: What is required when carrying a passenger on a motorcycle?

options.text: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
Only have one set of footrests.
Not encourage the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other motorists that a passenger is on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat large enough for two riders. It must have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear as you do.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car:

options.text: You are likely riding in the best position to be seen.
You may not be seen unless the driver uses their side mirror.
The driver will most likely assume you are there.
You are discouraging other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not be seen unless the driver uses their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors much more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: To control your motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Sit with your arms propping you up rather than steering.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Allow your feet to hang off the footrests.
Sit so far back that you must stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance in turns. Sit forward enough to use your arms for steering, not for holding yourself up. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: To provide the best protection, a helmet should:

options.text: Have a few cracks.
Not be certified.
Have frayed straps.
Fit snugly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: What is the single most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
Wear shorts.
Wear sneakers.
Wear goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened is the single most effective way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, they should:

options.text: Lean with you as you lean.
Hold onto the seat.
Sit as far back on the seat as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with you as you lean.
questions.explanation: Passengers should lean with the operator. They should sit as far forward as comfortable without crowding you. They should hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: For the best protection, riding gloves should be made of:

options.text: Leather.
Wool.
Polyester.
Silk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another strong, durable material. This gives you proper protection.

questions.question: An approved helmet should:

options.text: Let you see to the sides as needed for safe riding.
Limit your side vision.
Usually be uncomfortable.
Have no markings or labels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let you see to the sides as needed for safe riding.
questions.explanation: Approved helmets let you see to the sides as needed for safe riding. Approved helmets have labels and markings with the manufacturer's name, instructions, and information about safety standards met.

questions.question: To reduce your risk of an accident, you should:

options.text: Try to blend in with traffic so other drivers don't notice you.
Only use turn signals when riding at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
Ride very close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to other road users. Use your turn signals, brake light, and correct lane position. Keep enough space between you and other vehicles. Look 12 seconds ahead. Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.question: You can increase your visibility by:

options.text: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.
Not using your turn signal.
Wearing dark clothing.
Waving at people.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright or reflective clothing. Add extra lights to your motorcycle. Use your turn signals. Flash your brake light when needed. These actions help other drivers see you.

questions.question: To get the most protection, choose a helmet that:

options.text: Fits loosely.
Meets U.S. DOT standards.
Has been in a previous crash.
Provides hearing protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state safety standards. The helmet should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: One benefit of regular motorcycle maintenance is:

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take very little time.
Maintenance costs very little.
Maintenance checks can prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A properly maintained motorcycle will continue to run like new. Make routine maintenance a regular part of your care plan.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Drag your feet to help with balance.
Point your toes downward.
Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
Keep your feet away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not drag your feet on the road. Do not point your toes down, as they may catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if needed.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Stay in the same part of the lane all the time.
Constantly change lane positions to keep other drivers out.
Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Not worry about where in the lane you ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: A danger of riding next to parked cars is:

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Other drivers may be looking for parking spots and driving slowly.
The road surface may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Riding next to parked cars is dangerous. A driver might pull out suddenly without looking. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Only the front brake.
Only the rear brake.
Both brakes.
Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time. Using both brakes together is the most effective way to stop.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs are white with black letters. They show rules like speed limits. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When approaching an object or uneven surface that you cannot avoid, you should:

options.text: Make sure the motorcycle is leaning to one side.
Speed up.
Swerve quickly.
Rise slightly off the seat to allow your legs to absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat to allow your legs to absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as possible. Keep the motorcycle upright. Rise off the seat a little so your legs can absorb the impact. Just before hitting the obstacle, roll on the throttle slightly to lift the front end.

questions.question: If the chain or belt of your motorcycle breaks, you will:

options.text: Experience a sudden increase in power to the rear wheel.
Experience a sudden loss of power to the rear wheel.
Experience a sudden loss of power to the front wheel.
Experience a sudden increase in power to the front wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experience a sudden loss of power to the rear wheel.
questions.explanation: If your chain or belt breaks, power to the rear wheel stops immediately.

questions.question: It is a good idea to wear reflective clothing:

options.text: At night.
During the day.
At dusk.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective and bright clothing anytime you ride. Crashes happen both day and night. Wear visible clothing at all times.

questions.question: For a person to be allowed to ride as a passenger:

options.text: They must be able to reach the footrests on both sides of the motorcycle while seated.
They must hold a motorcycle license.
They must be willing to operate the motorcycle if the operator becomes too tired.
They must be older than 18 years old.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must be able to reach the footrests on both sides of the motorcycle while seated.
questions.explanation: A passenger can only ride if they can reach the footrests on both sides while sitting on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an example of a slippery surface?

options.text: A gravel road
A patch of leaves
An ice patch
Dry concrete

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry concrete
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted road markings, and metal plates. Dry concrete is not slippery.

questions.question: Most crashes occur in broad daylight. To be more visible, you should:

options.text: Wear brightly-colored clothing.
Wear darkly-colored clothing.
Ride without your headlight.
Ride in a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear brightly-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright clothing when riding, even in daylight.

questions.question: Your motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
More easily seen than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as noticeable as a car's brake light. Flashing your brake light before you slow down or stop can help other drivers see you.

questions.question: During the day, you should:

options.text: Not ride with your headlight on.
Ride with your headlight on, but only if it is cloudy.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Use your headlight if you think it helps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Always ride with your headlight on, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to notice you.
